title: Agent Lifecycle Receipt Submit Request
description: ALR-1102 Route 4 request (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:695-722): POST .../agent-lifecycle/run-plans/{run_plan_ref}/receipts. Submits indexed, content-free receipts against a Route-3-issued plan and consumes its one-time nonce. A raw prediction/output/input/gold value is never accepted here -- only index/item_ref/outcome/rescorability_state per receipt (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:711-718). This document is closed (additionalProperties:false) with exactly three top-level properties, so it is structurally impossible for a client to supply a denominator/completeness field alongside the receipts: Backend derives every accepted accounting count exclusively from the plan it already issued (owner accounting decision, runs/agent-lifecycle-contract-integration/OWNER_DECISION_ACCOUNTING_20260809.md) -- the two fields that decision deleted from this route entirely (no consumer required the first; the second carried a privacy/equality-oracle risk with no offsetting Part 1 use, PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:1452) do not appear anywhere in this document, and neither does the field this route's own request-body denominator poison probe targets. The named failure mutation this story proves by hand is exactly 'permit client expected_count as a denominator': widening this schema's properties to accept one is the guard this corpus's receipt_submit_client_expected_count_denominator_rejected case exists to kill. `Idempotency-Key` (required header, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{31,127}$) and `nonce` consumption/replay state are Backend/route concerns outside this JSON body (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:701, :722); a missing/malformed header is service_invalid (corpus cases receipt_submit_missing_idempotency_key, idempotency_key_malformed_pattern_rejected), not schema-decidable. Each receipt's rescorability_state is outcome-conditioned (closes Opus P1-4): for produced/cached/fallback it may be available/unavailable/unknown; for failed/excluded, available is invalid -- schema-decidable via if/then on these two sibling fields per receipt (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:718). This is the Schema half of guard-killing mutation #14 (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:1152): removing/weakening this if/then is exactly what corpus cases receipt_available_on_failed and receipt_available_on_excluded exist to catch.

nonce.description: The one-time issue nonce from Route 3. Request-only on this route -- never echoed in the response (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:708, :736).

receipts.description: 1..expected_count; unique indexes; maxItems=10000 beta ceiling (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:709). Omitted expected indexes become missing. The upper bound tied to the plan's own expected_count and cross-entry index/item_ref uniqueness are service_invalid (corpus cases receipt_duplicate_index, receipt_item_ref_mismatch, receipt_index_out_of_universe) -- they require comparing this array against the previously-issued plan or across its own sibling entries, not decidable from this document alone (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:971). minItems/maxItems and each receipt's own closed, outcome-conditioned shape ARE schema-decidable and enforced here.

index.description: Integer in the issued universe (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:715); the upper bound is the plan's own expected_count and is service_invalid, not schema-decidable here.

item_ref.description: Exact opaque evidence_item ref issued for that index (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:716).

rescorability_state.description: Remains client-attested (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:718). Outcome-conditioned by the allOf/if/then below: available is invalid when outcome is failed or excluded.
